article_text:
Japanese animated sensation “ Chiikawa the Movie: The Secret of the Mermaid Island ” maintained a commanding grip on the South Korean box office over the weekend of Oct. 23–25, capturing nearly 45% of nationwide ticket revenue in its fourth frame.

According to data from KOBIS, the tracking service operated by the Korean Film Council, the Toho-distributed fantasy release took in $2.5 million from 320,293 admissions across 1,115 screens, accounting for 44.7% of the weekend market.

Related Stories

Elizabeth Banks Officially Set to Play Karen Read in Amazon Series

'Things We Never Got Over' Amazon Series Adds Six to Cast

Directed by Kei Oikawa and adapted from the popular manga by Nagano, the fantasy feature tracks the small protagonist and companions journeying to a scenic coastal island before uncovering a sinister local mystery. Driven by enduring youth and family turnout, the animated blockbuster pushed its cumulative South Korean haul to $17.5 million from 2,248,137 total admissions since launching on Sep. 30.

Popular on Variety

Director Hur Jin-ho’s political thriller “ The Assassin(s) ” held second place, earning $520,822 from 68,241 admissions across 730 screens to capture 9.2% of the frame. Distributed by Hive Media Corp, the period drama reconstructs the August 15, 1974 assassination attempt on President Park Chung-hee and stars Yu Hae-jin, Park Hae-il, and Lee Min-ho investigating irregularities surrounding the inquiry into the death of First Lady Yuk Young-soo.

The production’s theatrical run continues against persistent political blowback and legal challenges, with conservative civic groups and bereaved family members lodging defamation complaints alleging historical distortion over its depiction of state involvement. Despite protests that previously prompted 19 film guilds to issue a joint statement defending cinematic freedom, the release lifted its cume to $25 million from 3,374,517 admissions since its Sep. 23 rollout.

CJ Entertainment’s psychological thriller “ Paradise Lost ” opened in third place, generating $502,962 from 66,699 admissions across 803 screens for an 8.9% market share. Directed and co-written by Yeon Sang-ho and starring Kim Hyun-joo and Bae Hyun-sung, the mystery follows a desperate mother navigating a closed religious community while searching for her missing son. Following its world premiere at Toronto and an Oct. 21 mid-week rollout, the title has accumulated $769,865 from 104,877 total admissions.

Warner Bros. and DC Studios’ “ Clayface ” debuted in fourth place, collecting $388,947 from 48,245 admissions across 655 screens for 6.9% of the market. Since opening on Oct. 21, the film has grossed $595,460 from 77,153 viewers.

CJ ENM’s gambling drama “Tazza: The Song of Beelzebub” took fifth place in its fifth weekend, taking in $371,743 from 46,919 admissions across 618 screens to claim 6.6% of receipts. Directed by Choi Kook-hee and starring Byun Yo-han, Noh Jae-won, and Ayaka Miyoshi, the fourth installment in the franchise pushed its gross to $15.3 million and stands on the brink of two million tickets at 1,999,477 admissions.

Plus M Entertainment’s period drama “Still Shining” opened in sixth place, earning $148,298 from 21,564 admissions across 562 screens. Directed by Song Il-gon and starring veteran actor Kim Hye-ja alongside Cha Mi-kyung, the drama traces the lifelong bond between two women who promised to sing together in Seoul during the Japanese colonial era. Counting mid-week business since its Oct. 21 debut, the release has taken $278,527 from 41,037 viewers.

Universal’s tentpole “The Odyssey” placed seventh in its twelfth weekend, drawing $164,558 from 20,189 admissions across 341 screens. Its cumulative haul reached $106.2 million from 12,311,245 admissions since opening on Aug. 5.

Amazon MGM Studios and Warner Bros.’ psychological thriller “Verity” opened in eighth place, pulling in $120,876 from 16,416 admissions across 458 screens and has grossed $178,096 from 25,190 admissions since its Oct. 22 bow.

Director Kore-eda Hirokazu’s live-action manga drama “Look Back” took ninth place in its third weekend, earning $126,854 from 15,624 admissions across 190 screens, lifting its cumulative total to $1 million from 131,051 admissions.

Rounding out the top 10 was domestic action thriller “Killing Time” with $82,439 from 11,244 admissions across 274 screens. Directed by Jang Jun-yeob and starring Ryu Hye-young and Nam Yoon-su, the film centers on a popular YouTube crew that collapses overnight after an accident claims a member’s life during a live broadcast; when they stage an extreme comeback stunt to regain fame, mysterious figures force them into a real, deadly survival game. Since its Oct. 21 release, the thriller has grossed $135,388 from 19,121 viewers.

The overall market collective gross for the weekend was $5.6 million, down from last week’s $6.7 million.

article_text:
Durng a fireside chat entitled “Every Pixel Will Be Generated” at Turin’s View Conference , an audience member asked Cristóbal Valenzuela, the co-CEO of generative AI startup Runway, whether AI could eventually replace human actors.

“Yeah, absolutely. I think it’s already happening in a way,” he replied, going on to describe AI as “a new medium of expression” and “a new medium of storytelling.”

Variety Nominated for 62 Arts & Entertainment Journalism Awards

His fellow speaker, Nvidia ‘s Richard Kerris, was somewhat more attached to existing arrangements. Earlier in the session, he had recalled a director’s argument that the spontaneity between a director and an actor, such as Marlon Brando improvising with a cat on the set of “The Godfather,” could never be prompted.

“That craft is something to behold, and I just think that that’s something that I don’t think we’ll ever lose,” said Kerris, Nvidia VP of developer relations and general manager of media and entertainment.

“Not now, but I think models are going to get probably to a point where you can probably direct them in a very similar way,” Valenzuela replied.

Kerris had also stressed that filmmaking still requires an understanding of character, composition and story. There is no “make movie button.”

“I wish,” joked Valenzuela.

A clear sense of what this might mean sits in Vaenzuela’s essay titled “It’s All About the Pixel Economy,” in which Valenzuela predicts that “the value of creating pixels is trending towards zero.” Eventually, he writes, the number of “seconds consumed” will converge with the number of “seconds generated.”

Presently, a film often takes hundreds of people to make and millions of people two hours to watch. Valenzuela imagines a future where audiences generate personalized entertainment as quickly as they consume it.

In another essay, “The Cost of a Frame,” Valenzuela charts a history of media through the cost of producing a credible frame. The relevant layer is the high production value content. It’s that tier in which Hollywood, and much of the conference’s professionals, work in.

“This is the last expensive layer,” he writes and AI, he makes the case, is collapsing the cost of producing it.

At the View fireside chat, Kerris frequently framed the resistance toward the technology as no different than the fears that previous tech advances stirred, including the emergence of computer-generated imagery. “The similarities of fear and rush to judgment on things is so similar to what I’ve seen in the past,” he said.

Jeff Kember, Nvidia’s principal technical evangelist for media, painted a similarly optimistic vision in his presentation, “Creative Control in the Age of AI Agents,” claiming that adoption is already widespread.

“There’s a whole bunch of people talking about how they’re using generative AI and then there’s also a bunch of people who aren’t talking about it and they’re not talking about it primarily because their legal team is not letting them talk about it,” he said. ‘But both people on each side of this fence are both using generative AI. I don’t know anyone who isn’t.”

Between sessions a number of VFX artists, game studio heads, and animation directors spoke less of fear and more of anger relating to something peculiar and unique to the generative models, namely the material used to train on in the first place.

Asked by Variety about the training data behind the models, Valenzuela said one of the “core misbeliefs” about AI was that “people thought AI was some sort of a database.”

“They’re not databases,” he said. “They’re learning from representation.”

It seems an unavoidable concern with the courts, the likely arbiter. In July, a federal judge approved Anthropic’s settlement of $1.5 billion with authors whose books were downloaded from pirate libraries. A prior ruling had found that using copyrighted works to train models could constitute fair use, while distinguishing that question from the company’s acquisition and retention of pirated copies. Meanwhile, there are a number of lawsuits against many of the biggest AI companies still going through the legal system. One is a proposed class action case by visual artists against Stability AI, Midjourney, DeviantArt and Runway itself. It alleges that their copyrighted work was used to develop the generative models without compensation or permission.

Taken together the talks from the companies leading the charge in AI at View Conference revealed a worldview whereby the cost of generating moving images approaches zero and at the least the traditional structures of production are fundamentally reshaped.

article_text:
10月24日、DOVER STREET MARKET GINZA 7Fにて、ロサンゼルスを拠点とするイギリス人写真家、ニック・ヘイムズのトークイベント&サイン会が行われる。

ニック・ヘイムズは、2001年から2026年にかけて作者が撮影した25年以上にわたる写真を収録した写真集 『 CHRONOGRAPH 』 でパートナーのリナ（Lina）と二人の子ども、フィリップ（Philipp）、ローレンス（Lawrence）との暮らしを記録した。それらは、没入感あふれるクロニクルとも言えるもの。450ページを超える紙面に約1,000点の写真を収録し、ロサンゼルスとニューヨークを行き来しながら、長年にわたるドキュメンタリーの視線を最も身近な存在へと向けている。本書は、aperture主催のParis Photo–Aperture PhotoBook Awards 2026、「 Photo Book Of The Year 」部門のショートリストにノミネートされた。

このトークイベントでは、本作の制作背景から、写真家の活動のほかにLittle Big Man Galleryを主宰するヘイムズにギャラリー運営、出版や日本との深い関係性について話を聞く。

また、10月20日〜11月1日の期間には 刊行記念展 （photographers’ gallery）も開催されるので、あわせて立ち寄りたい。

タイトル

CHRONOGRAPH TALK AND BOOK SIGNING WITH NICK HAYMES

場所

DOVER STREET MARKET GINZA 7F ROSE BAKERY （東京都中央区銀座６丁目９−５ ギンザコマツ 西館 ７階）

日程

2026年10月24日（土）

時間

15:00〜16:30

料金

無料 ※要予約（一部立ち見あり）

URL

https://peatix.com/event/5225553

editorial_title_zh: 2026都灵艺术周，今日展览与活动地图
editorial_excerpt_zh: 2026都灵艺术周蓄势待发：通过 Untitled Association 的地图，我们为您推荐今日丰富多彩的展览与表演路线，从波河沿岸一直延伸至市中心。本文来源于……
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "借 2026 年 Artissima 艺博会开幕之际（展期为 10 月 30 日至 11 月 1 日），Untitled Association 将带您探索都灵艺术周期间不容错过的展览、活动和项目。我们为行业专业人士、艺术爱好者或普通游客规划了多条参观路线，串联起各大博物馆、机构空间、私人画廊以及独立空间。", "links": [{"text": "Artissima", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/tag/artissima/"}, {"text": "Untitled Association", "url": "https://www.instagram.com/untitledassociation/"}, {"text": "Torino Art Week", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/tag/torino-art-week/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "行程始于万基列塔（Vanchiglietta）区，参观乔治·格里法基金会（Fondazione Giorgio Griffa），随后沿波河（Po）前行，前往 Metroquadro 和 Roccatre 画廊。穿过维 Vittorio Emanuele I 桥，我们抵达金兹堡花园（Giardino Ginzburg）附近，那里坐落着都灵国家高山博物馆（Museo Nazionale della Montagna CAI Torino）。路线继续向市中心延伸，途经翁贝托一世桥（ponte Umberto I），在此我们会遇到 Photo & Contemporary 画廊以及 CAMERA——意大利摄影中心。最后，我们在紧邻马达马宫（Palazzo Madama）的市中心结束一天的行程，参观韦伯画廊（Weber & Weber）。如果愿意，晚上 19 点还可以在奥罗拉（Aurora）街区观赏 Paint It Black 的一场表演。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "2026都灵艺术周：今日活动", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们从万基列塔出发，距离玛格丽特女王广场（Piazale Regina Margherita）不远，首先来到乔治·格里法基金会，观看乔治·格里法（Giorgio Griffa）与张恩利的双人展。展览中，两人作品交替呈现，勾勒出一种动态的展示，构建出节奏、靠拢与分歧。一方面，格里法将绘画自身智慧的显现交托给裸露的画布、笔触、色彩与寂静：不去表现世界，而是倾听并揭示其动态与能量。另一方面，张恩利则用画笔定格了本质与情感领域，那些感知、记忆和共鸣得以放大、转化并揭示现实的面貌与内涵的空间。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/01_FONDAZIONE-GRIFFA.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Giorgio Griffa, Campo arancione, 2026. Acquerello su carta (22x30cm) – Courtesy Fondazione Giorgio Griffa, Torino", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们将在本周五（10 月 30 日）重返该地区，出席卡罗尔·拉马档案库（Archivio Carol Rama）全新运营与文化总部的落成典礼，并参观卡罗尔·拉马（Carol Rama）与古列尔莫·卡斯特利（Guglielmo Castelli）的展览。新址位于安多尔诺街（via Andorno），坐落在一个历史建筑群内，这里本身就已经是一座当代艺术的小型微型社区，毗邻乔治·格里法基金会、马尔科·加斯蒂尼档案库（Archivio Marco Gastini）以及路易吉·迈诺尔菲（Luigi Mainolfi）、埃莉萨·西吉切利（Elisa Sighicelli）、格拉齐娅·托德里（Grazia Toderi）和吉尔伯托·佐里奥（Gilberto Zorio）的工作室。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/02_ARCHIVIO-CAROL-RAMA.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "Guglielmo Castelli, Senza titolo, 2023 – Ph. Nicola Morittu – Courtesy l’artista, Mendes Wood DM, São Paulo, Brussels, New York, Paris e Sylvia Kouvali, London, Piraeus", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "不远处，位于勒吉纳玛格丽特大街（Corso Regina Margherita）1:1 空间的埃尔曼诺·布罗西奥（Ermanno Brosio）、卢卡·F·费雷罗（Luca F. Ferrero）和莫扎特·莱特（Mozzarella Light）群展 1:1 Exhibition 正式开幕。艺术家们展出了一系列全新作品，其介入与空间紧密对话，在一个致力于研究和创意实验的环境中，充当着能够激发全新感知过程的装置。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们沿着尼科洛·马基雅维利波河沿岸（Lungo Po Niccolò Machiavelli）前行，来到接下来的两站：Metroquadro 和 Roccatre 画廊。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Metroquadro 画廊带来的莫妮卡·罗林斯（Monique Rollins）个展，为都灵公众提供了一个契机，在艺术家享有极高国际知名度之际深入了解其创作探索。她近期参加了由罗伯托·马斯特罗扬尼（Roberto Mastroianni）策展的第 61 届威尼斯双年展，并举办了题为 We are Infinite Beings with Infinite Possibilities 的个展。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/04_METROQUADRO.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "Monique Rollins, The Excitement, 2026. Carboncino, acrilico e olio su tela (76x66cm) – Courtesy l’artista e Metroquadro, Torino", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "不远处的 Roccatre 画廊呈现了群展《但愿穿过村庄的街道……》（Ma per le vie del borgo…），这是一个完全致力于都灵著名街区博尔戈努沃（Borgo Nuovo）的艺术身份与创作活力的项目，该画廊便坐落于此。该展览旨在还原这片土地的深厚底蕴：几十年来，这里远不止是一个城市背景，而是一个真正的露天实验室，也是数代创意人士的交汇点。展览汇聚了菲利斯·卡索拉蒂（Felice Casorati）、伊塔洛·克雷莫纳（Italo Cremona）、朱利奥·保利尼（Giulio Paolini）和萨尔沃（Salvo）等曾在该街区生活和工作过的大师级艺术家的作品，以及至今仍在此居住和创作的当代艺术家的作品，见证了这里从未中断的文化活力。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/05_ROCCATRE.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Claudio Rotta Loria, Interferenza-full", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们穿过维多利亚埃马努埃莱一世桥，前往接下来的几站。沿途正好在这座古老的桥上，我们向您推荐约瑟夫·科苏斯（Joseph Kosuth）的艺术灯光作品《双重过境》（Doppio passaggio）。霓虹灯文字重现了伊塔洛·卡尔维诺（Italo Calvino）的《看不见的城市》以及弗里德里希·尼采（Friedrich Nietzsche）的《查拉图斯特拉如是说》中的两段文字；两段文本长度相当，并对立放置，共同阐发了将桥梁作为沟通媒介的隐喻。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/06_LUCE1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Joseph Kosuth, Doppio Passaggio Torino, 2001 – Ph. Andrea Rossetti", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "朝着金兹堡花园和卡普奇尼山圣玛丽亚教堂（Chiesa di Santa Maria del Monte dei Cappuccini）方向前行，在卡普奇尼山（Monte dei Cappuccini）上，我们还会遇到雷贝卡·霍恩（Rebecca Horn）为“艺术灯光”（Luci d’Artista）创作的灯光装置《微小蓝色精灵》（Piccoli spiriti blu）。这束光由七十二个大小不一的霓虹圆环组成，最初安装在格兰马德雷教堂（Gran Madre）周围，后来移至卡普奇尼山，环绕着教堂并一直延伸至前修道院的一个侧翼。在这两个地点，该作品都通过营造一种带有虚幻色调的悬浮氛围，改变了人们对空间的感知。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/07_LUCE2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Rebecca Horn, piccoli spiriti blu, 1999 – Ph. Gianluca Minuto", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "步行不远，我们便来到了都灵国立山地博物馆CAI Torino（Museo Nazionale della Montagna CAI Torino），参观由安德烈·莱尔达（Andrea Lerda）和琳达·科蒂诺（Linda Cottino）策划的群展《零度：超越性别的山地》（Grado Zero. La montagna oltre i generi）。该展览立足于当代艺术作品与历史资料之间的对话，旨在打破霸权式的男子气概，审视山地的宗法世系，并反思宗法制度与气候危机之间的关系。同时，它也作为一个重新出发的空间，旨在将男性与女性之间结盟的理念常态化，并借此引领人们走向一种可实现的乌托邦：一个超越性别的山地。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在这种愿景下，山地不再仅仅是被征服和开发的土地，而是需要栖息、守护和重新构想的空间。它成为了关系性后人类伦理的土壤，能够识别身体、社群和生命形式之间的相互依存关系；重新将共生（commoning）、关怀生命以及共同家园的意义置于核心地位。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/08_MUSEO-CAI.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Super Taus，《Super Taus》(Untitled 1)，2014年。彩色有声病毒视频（2′ 16″）– © Super Taus", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "此外，不容错过的还有由登山史学家兼记者罗伯托·曼托瓦尼（Roberto Mantovani）策划的群展《东方地图集》（Atlante Orientale）。该展览源于对博物馆档案馆及意大利阿尔卑斯俱乐部国家图书馆所藏文献的深入普查，其中涌现出各种见证、影像、物品、地图、卷宗和原始文献，勾勒出意大利在亚洲长达半个多世纪的探险历程。展览追溯了自19世纪末至1954年意大利国家登山队历史性首登K2期间，意大利旅行家、学者、摄影师和登山者的足迹，并将其置于地理与登山探险更广阔的国际背景之中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们穿过翁贝托一世桥（Ponte Umberto I）回到波河对岸，继续前往市中心的下一站。在加富尔花园（Giardini Cavour）、艾乌奥拉花园（Giardino Aiuola）和瓦尔多·富西广场（Piazzale Valdo Fusi）附近，紧凑地分布着Photo & Contemporary画廊、都灵摄影中心（CAMERA – Centro Italiano per la Fotografia）以及温贝托·贝纳皮画廊（Galleria Umberto Benappi）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Photo & Contemporary画廊为庆祝成立30周年，推出了《光与影：第二部分》（Light & Shadows. Part Two），展出了不同愿景的交汇与互动。展览的第一部分侧重于“影”（SHADOWS），曾在4月至5月期间推出首展，聚焦身体与黑暗的主题，这也是对Exposed艺术节主题《脱光》（Mettersi a nudo）的致敬。而在作为第二部分的“光”（LIGHTS）中，则绽放出都市风景令人惊叹的色彩。此外，该画廊还负责策划卡尔利纳广场（Piazza Carlina）知名NH精选酒店（NH Collection）庭院画廊（Galleria della Corte）举办的《重塑风景》（Reinventing the Landscape）系列展。该系列展旨在庆祝酒店开业10周年，通过将德国艺术家托马斯·弗雷德（Thomas Wrede）和尼尔斯-乌多（Nils-Udo）的作品进行对比，在摄影和观念艺术之间，为人类、自然与风景感知之间的联系提供了一种新颖且富有暗示性的反思。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/09A_PHOTO-AND-CO.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "乔治·鲁斯（Georges Rousse），Chambery，2018年 – © Georges Rousse", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "不远处的CAMERA – Centro Italiano per la Fotografia呈现了摄影师莱蒂齐亚·巴塔利亚（Letizia Battaglia）的个展《Letizia Battaglia. Works 1970-2020》。该展览由沃尔特·瓜达尼尼（Walter Guadagnini）策划，由都灵摄影中心与网球场美术馆（Jeu de Paume）联合制作，并得到了莱蒂齐亚·巴塔利亚档案库（Archivio Letizia Battaglia）的合作支持。展览通过200多幅影像回溯了这位西西里女摄影师的生平与创作，展现了她丰富的艺术探索以及对社会和公民事务的不懈承诺。展线不仅呈现了她专注于黑手党岁月的著名摄影作品，还对其贯穿整个创作生涯的主题进行了广泛梳理。此外，展出的22本巴塔利亚曾参与合作——甚至在某些情况下亲自创办并主编——的杂志以及一部关于其生平的纪录片，进一步丰富了对其生平与职业生涯的叙事。", article_text:
In occasione dell’edizione 2026 di Artissima , che aprirà al pubblico dal 30 ottobre al 1° novembre, Untitled Association vi accompagna alla scoperta di mostre, eventi e iniziative da non perdere nei giorni della Torino Art Week , con itinerari pensati per professionisti del settore, appassionati d’arte o semplici curiosi, tra musei, spazi istituzionali, gallerie private e spazi indipendenti.

La giornata inizia nella zona di Vanchiglietta con la visita alla Fondazione Giorgio Griffa , per poi proseguire lungo il fiume Po in direzione delle gallerie Metroquadro e Roccatre . Attraversando il ponte Vittorio Emanuele I, raggiungiamo l’area del Giardino Ginzburg, nei pressi del quale si trova il Museo Nazionale della Montagna CAI Torino . Il percorso continua verso il centro città, passando per il ponte Umberto I, dove incontriamo la galleria Photo & Contemporary , CAMERA – Centro Italiano per la Fotografia . Concludiamo infine la giornata in pieno centro, nei pressi di Palazzo Madama, con la visita alla galleria Weber & Weber . Volendo poi, alle 19, la serata può iniziare nel quartiere Aurora, con una performance da Paint It Black .

Torino Art Week 2026: gli appuntamenti di oggi

Si parte in Vanchiglietta, poco distanti da Piazzale Regina Margherita, con la Fondazione Giorgio Griffa e la bipersonale di Giorgio Griffa e Zhang Enli . In mostra, l’alternanza dei loro lavori delinea una manifestazione dinamica, costruisce ritmi, avvicinamenti e scarti. Da un lato Griffa affida alle tele nude, al segno, al colore e ai silenzi il compito di lasciar emergere l’intelligenza propria della pittura: non rappresentare il mondo, ma ascoltarne e svelarne le dinamiche e le energie. Dall’altro Zhang Enli con il pennello fissa essenze e campi emotivi, spazi in cui percezioni, memorie e risonanze amplificano, trasformano e svelano aspetti e risvolti della realtà.

Torneremo in zona il prossimo venerdì, 30 ottobre, per l’inaugurazione della nuova sede operativa e culturale dell’ Archivio Carol Rama con una mostra di Carol Rama e Guglielmo Castelli . In via Andorno, inserito in un complesso storico che è già una piccola cittadella dell’arte contemporanea, con la Fondazione Giorgio Griffa, appunto, l’Archivio Marco Gastini e gli studi di Luigi Mainolfi, Elisa Sighicelli, Grazia Toderi e Gilberto Zorio .

Poco distante, da 1:1 in Corso Regina Margherita, vi segnaliamo l’apertura della collettiva 1:1 Exhibition di Ermanno Brosio , Luca F. Ferrero e Mozzarella Light . Con una selezione di opere inedite, gli interventi degli artisti sono concepiti in stretto dialogo con lo spazio e fungono da dispositivi capaci di generare nuovi processi di percezione all’interno di un ambiente dedicato alla ricerca e alla sperimentazione creativa.

Percorriamo il Lungo Po Niccolò Machiavelli fino alle prossime due tappe: le gallerie Metroquadro e Roccatre .

La galleria Metroquadro con la personale di Monique Rollins offre al pubblico torinese l’occasione di approfondire la ricerca dell’artista in un momento di particolare visibilità internazionale, segnato dalla sua presenza alla 61° Biennale di Venezia, con la personale We are Infinite Beings with Infinite Possibilities curata da Roberto Mastroianni .

Poco distante, la galleria Roccatre presenta la collettiva Ma per le vie del borgo… un progetto interamente dedicato all’identità artistica e al fermento creativo del celebre quartiere torinese Borgo Nuovo all’interno del quale la galleria stessa ha la propria sede. L’esposizione nasce con la volontà di restituire l’essenza profonda di un territorio che, nel corso dei decenni, è stato molto più di uno sfondo urbano, un vero e proprio laboratorio a cielo aperto e un punto di incontro per generazioni di creativi. La mostra riunisce opere di artisti storici del calibro di Felice Casorati, Italo Cremona, Giulio Paolini e Salvo , che hanno vissuto e lavorato nel quartiere e artisti contemporanei, che vi risiedono e operano ancora oggi, testimoniando così una vitalità culturale che non si è mai interrotta.

Attraversiamo il ponte Vittorio Emanuele I in direzione delle nostre prossime tappe. Lungo il percorso proprio sull’antico ponte vi segnaliamo la Luce d’Artista Doppio passaggio di Joseph Kosuth . Le scritte in neon riproducono due brani tratti da Le città invisibili di Italo Calvino e da Così parl ò Zarathustra di Friedrich Nietzsche; di uguale estensione e posti uno di fronte all’altro, entrambi i testi sviluppano la metafora del ponte come veicolo di comunicazione.

Verso il giardino di Ginzburg e la Chiesa di Santa Maria del Monte dei Cappuccini, incontriamo inoltre, in Monte dei Cappuccini, l’intervento luminoso Piccoli spiriti blu di Rebecca Horn ancora per le Luci d’Artista. La luce è composta da settantadue cerchi di neon di dimensioni diverse, installati inizialmente attorno alla chiesa della Gran Madre, e poi sul Monte dei Cappuccini, dove circondano la chiesa estendendosi fino a un’ala dell’ex convento. In entrambe le sedi, l’opera contribuisce a modificare la percezione dello spazio creando un’atmosfera di sospensione dai toni irreali.

A due passi raggiungiamo il Museo Nazionale della Montagna CAI Torino e la collettiva Grado Zero. La montagna oltre i generi a cura di Andrea Lerda e Linda Cottino . La mostra, fondata sul dialogo tra opere contemporanee e materiali storici, muove dalla necessità di decentrare la maschilità egemonica, interrogare le genealogie patriarcali della montagna e riflettere sulla relazione tra patriarcato e crisi climatica. Al tempo stesso, si propone come uno spazio di ripartenza, in cui normalizzare l’idea di alleanza tra maschile e femminile e attraverso il quale guidare il passo verso un’utopia realizzabile: una montagna oltre i generi.

In questa prospettiva, la montagna non è più soltanto terra da conquistare e sfruttare, ma spazio da abitare, custodire e ripensare. Diventa il terreno di un’etica post-umana relazionale, capace di riconoscere l’interdipendenza tra corpi, comunità e forme di vita; di rimettere al centro il senso del commoning, della cura della vita e della casa comune.

Da non perdere inoltre la collettiva Atlante Orientale curata dallo storico dell’alpinista e giornalista Roberto Mantovani . L’esposizione nasce da un’approfondita ricognizione negli archivi del Museo e nella documentazione conservata dalla Biblioteca Nazionale del Club Alpino Italiano, da cui emergono testimonianze, immagini, oggetti, carte geografiche, volumi e documenti originali capaci di ricostruire oltre mezzo secolo di esplorazioni italiane in Asia. Il percorso racconta infatti la presenza di viaggiatori, studiosi, fotografi e alpinisti italiani dalla fine dell’Ottocento fino alla storica spedizione nazionale italiana al K2 del 1954, inserendola nel più ampio contesto internazionale delle esplorazioni geografiche e alpinistiche.

Ritorniamo al di là del Po attraversando ponte Umberto I per muoverci verso il centro con le prossime tappe. Intorno ai giardini Cavour, il Giardino Aiuola e Piazzale Valdo Fusi, troviamo vicinissime la galleria Photo & Contemporary, il centro Camera – Centro Italiano per la Fotografia e la Galleria Umberto Benappi.

La galleria Photo & Contemporary con Light & Shadows. Part Two , presentata per i 30 anni di attività, espone l’incontro e l’interazione tra visioni diverse. La prima sezione della mostra, sul versante SHADOWS, aveva presentato in Aprile/Maggio una prima esposizione sul tema del corpo e dell’oscurità, anche in omaggio al titolo Mettersi a nudo del festival Exposed. Con LIGHTS, secondo appuntamento, esplodono invece i colori sorprendenti dei paesaggi urbani. La galleria inoltre porta avanti la curatela della rassegna Reinventing the Landscape ospitata nella Galleria della Corte del prestigioso NH Collection in Piazza Carlina. La rassegna celebra i 10 anni dell’hotel mettendo a confronto le opere degli artisti tedeschi Thomas Wrede e Nils-Udo . Tra la fotografia e l’arte concettuale il progetto offre un’inedita e suggestiva riflessione sul legame tra uomo, natura e percezione del paesaggio.

Poco distante Camera – Centro Italiano per la Fotografia presenta la monografica Letizia Battaglia. Works 1970-2020 . Curata da Walter Guadagnini e coprodotta dal centro torinese e Jeu de Paume , in collaborazione con l’ Archivio Letizia Battaglia , l’esposizione ripercorre la vita e l’opera della fotografa siciliana attraverso oltre 200 immagini, restituendo la ricchezza della sua ricerca artistica e il suo costante impegno sociale e civile. Il percorso presenta le celebri fotografie dedicate agli anni della mafia, ma offre anche un’ampia panoramica sui temi che hanno attraversato tutta la sua produzione. Ad ampliare il racconto della sua vicenda umana e professionale contribuiscono 22 riviste con cui Battaglia collaborò – e che, in alcuni casi, fondò e diresse – e un docu-film dedicato alla sua vita.

La Project Room di Camera ospiterà invece Davide Tranchina con Light-years Away , una mostra personale dedicata a una delle figure più influenti della fotografia italiana contemporanea. Organizzata in collaborazione con la Galleria Studio G7 di Bologna e curata da Walter Guadagnini , la mostra ripercorre oltre vent’anni del percorso creativo dell’artista bolognese, attraverso una selezione di opere che abbracciano alcuni dei momenti più significativi della sua carriera, per una riflessione continua sull’immagine fotografica, sui suoi processi di costruzione e sul rapporto – mai univoco – tra fotografia e realtà.

Eccoci arrivati in Centro nei pressi di Palazzo Madama per la nostra ultima tappa: la galleria Weber & Weber e la bipersonale How slowly can I write? di Federica Patera e Andrea Sbra Perego a cura di Barbara Pavan . Un nuovo progetto espositivo in cui parole, filo e tessuto convergono e si trasformano, dando vita a opere che interrogano il nostro rapporto con il linguaggio, la materia e il tempo. Qui la scrittura si allontana dalla velocità della comunicazione per diventare gesto, presenza e spazio da attraversare.

Poco distante da Palazzo Madama, in Via Po, vi segnaliamo la luce d’artista Palomar di Giulio Paolini , composta da sagome luminose in forma di corpi celesti che si succedono in senso prospettico tra i palazzi di Torino. La sequenza è presieduta da un funambolo che guarda l’intera costellazione tenendo in mano un cerchio e due ellissi mentre sta in equilibrio su un triplice tondo che racchiude a sua volta una serie di orbite. Nell’interrogare le relazioni tra autore e opera, l’atto della visione è un tema ricorrente del lavoro di Paolini e la scelta di Palomar per la sua Luce è quindi particolarmente significativa: il funambolo con cui culmina l’opera si incarica di rappresentare l’artista, lo scrittore, il personaggio e l’uomo – tutti gli uomini – nella ricerca del senso ultimo delle cose.

Per una tappa fuori porta vi segnaliamo inoltre la mostra collettiva Desiderio | Atto Terzo inaugurata domenica, 25 ottobre, presso la galleria Soci é t é Interludio a Cambiano (Torino), con un testo critico di Giulia De Giorgi . L’esposizione rappresenta il terzo capitolo del progetto curatoriale dedicato al tema del desiderio, mettendo in dialogo dodici tra maestri storici ed esponenti dell’arte contemporanea.

Prima di lasciarci vi diamo un ultimo appuntamento serale, oggi alle 19, in via Buscalioni, quartiere Aurora, con la performance She is the one lying on the bottomless bottom. The Space of the Tongue di Ambra Pittoni con Francesca Ugolini , Vera di Lecce e le musiche di Federico Chiari , presentata in anteprima da Paint It Black , all’interno del programma di Artissima.

L’evento è il penultimo capitolo del progetto She the One lying on the Bottomless Bottom. The Space of the Tongue , che indaga il linguaggio come spazio di frattura, esaurimento e riverbero, celebrandoli come possibili stati di grazia della nostra epoca. Cerca la relazione tra oscurità e processi di conoscenza, immaginando un continuo movimento tra il dentro e il fuori. La grotta, ambiente geologico da sempre associato a dimensioni oracolari ed extra-mondane, incontra la bocca, in cui la lingua, dal suo antro buio, incorpora ed ex-corpora il mondo.

L’itinerario di martedì, 27 ottobre

article_text:
⁠Jurandir Filho ⁠, ⁠ Rogério Montanare ⁠, ⁠ Thiago Siqueira ⁠ e ⁠ Fernanda Bermoltz ⁠ conversam sobre “ Resident Evil “, a nova adaptação da popular série de jogos de videogames. Zach Cregger, diretor do sucesso recente “A Hora do Mal”, comandou e escreveu a história. Ele acertou? É o melhor filme da franquia? Na história, um entregador de medicamentos (Austin Abrams) se vê em uma luta desesperada pela sobrevivência contra criaturas mutantes e sedentas de sangue.

Single Image competition (Previously Open competition)

The Single Image competition celebrates the power of a standalone photograph. Enter your best single images - you could win $5,000, a range of top Sony Digital Imaging equipment plus benefit from international media exposure.

Free to enter and open to anyone submitting single images taken in 2026

Enter up to three single images for free

Ten diverse categories to enter

Awards category winners plus up to 15 shortlisted photographers per category

One overall winner receives the Single Image Competition Winner title

Please see 'Rules' below for full image eligibility criteria

Deadline is 5 January, 2027 at 16.00 GMT

Want to enter more than three images? Buy image bundles and submit as many photographs as you like. More information is available in your account.

PRIZES

Overall Winner

Category Winner

Shortlist

Win $5,000 (USD)

**Might be digital depending on position

Rules

The Single Image competition celebrates the power of a standalone photograph across ten (10) categories. Photographers should consider the category description when entering their work. Judges are looking for good composition, creativity and clear photographs.

If you enter the Single Image competition, you can also enter the Series competition. Entrants choosing to submit work across both Single Image and Series competitions must choose work originating from different bodies of work.

1.1 By entering the Competition You hereby accept these Competition Rules and the Terms and Conditions.

1.2.1 The Competition is free to enter.

1.2.2 The Single Image competition is open to all members of the public.

1.3 Entries must be submitted by 5 January, 2027 - 16.00 GMT.

1.4 By entering the Competition, You agree and acknowledge that the World Photography Organisation is permitted to receive Your registration data. All personal information will be used by the World Photography Organisation in accordance with its Privacy Policy.

1.5 If you enter the Single Image competition, you can also enter the Series competition. Entrants choosing to submit work across both Single Image and Series competitions must choose work originating from different bodies of work.

2. To enter, you must upload your image via the World Photography Organisation Website ( www.worldphoto.org ) or any of the official Sony World Photography Awards’ websites and follow the on-screen instructions carefully.

2.1 Images must be taken in 2026 and entries should be based on the Categories outlined, information on which can be found on the Website. Entrants can submit a photograph that has been taken, entered in another competition, won an award, or been published in books, magazines, newspapers, online and printed editorials, self-published websites, and gallery exhibitions between 1 January 2026 and 5 January 2027.

2.2 Images should be no smaller than 1MB and no larger than 5MB. Images should be JPEG files. All images must be saved in the sRGB colour model.

3.1 Entries will be judged between January 6 and January 31, 2027.

3.2 A shortlist of up to fifteen (15) photographers from each category and category winners will be selected and announced prior to April 2027; the overall winner will be announced in April 2027.

3.3 The individual category winners and the Single Image competition winner of the Sony World Photography Awards, will be voted for by the Judges and notified by email.

3.4 The decision of the Judges and the World Photography Organisation is final and no negotiation will be entered into with respect to any such decision.

3.5 Each Entrant can submit up to three images for free. The images entered can be entered in different categories or all images can be entered into a single category. Judging will be based on the single image and not the series of images.

3.5.2. During the judging process successful entries may be moved to a different category to the category they originally entered into. The decision will be made at the discretion of the judging panel. Successful entrants will be notified of the change over email.

4. Your Entry may feature manipulation, but where Entries are manipulated, the extent of which must be described in the image description section when submitting. For the avoidance of doubt, all Entries must originally be from either an analogue or digital photograph which may have then been manipulated. Computer generated content cannot be the origin of the Entry. Should a question arise through the judging process regarding the extent of your Entry’s manipulation you may be requested to submit the original photograph and image file to verify.

4.1 The World Photography Organisation reserves the right, in its sole discretion, to disqualify and remove any entry that does not comply with the following requirements, even after the entry is submitted on the Website. You warrant and represent, in respect of each entry submitted by You (“Entry”), as follows:

4.1.1 You are the sole owner and author of each Entry

4.1.2 You have the right to make Your Entry available to the Competition

4.1.3 Each Entry does not contain personally identifiable information about You or any other person(s)

4.1.4 Each Entry does not contain any infringing, threatening, false, misleading, abusive, harassing, libellous-, defamatory, vulgar, obscene, scandalous, inflammatory, pornographic or profane content

4.1.5 Each Entry does not contain any material that could constitute or encourage conduct which would be considered a criminal offence, give rise to civil liability, or otherwise violate any law

4.1.6 Each Entry does not infringe upon the copyrights, trademarks, contract rights, or any other intellectual property rights of any third person or entity, or violate any person’s rights of privacy or publicity, including:

4.1.6.1 trademarks owned by third parties

4.1.6.2 copyrighted materials owned by third parties (including movie dialogue or musical compositions)

4.1.6.3 names, likenesses, voices or other characteristics identifying celebrities or other public figures, living or dead

4.1.7 Entries which contain any commercial content that promotes any product or service other than that of the World Photography Organisation .

4.1.8 Entries containing screen credits

4.1.9 No animals were harmed, manipulated or distressed in the making of the image.

This includes, but is not limited to:

Deliberately disturbing or provoking an animal to capture a reaction

Using tape lures or decoys to attract animals or trigger a behaviour

Live baiting of any kind

Using flash photography on nocturnal birds

Failing to adhere to applicable laws, rules and permissions when working with wildlife and in natural environments, for example with protected species or protected environments

4.1.10 Archival images may be used when creating new work where any usage maintains compliance with clause 2. All archival images must be used with the required permissions. Usage of archival images must be stated in the description.

4.1.11 Drone usage must comply with the laws, rules, and permissions of the country in which the image was taken. The Promoter may request proof of permissions where applicable.

4.2 You agree to fully indemnify the World Photography Organisation in respect of all royalties, fees and any other monies owing to any person by reason of Your breaching any of the foregoing.

4.3 You confirm that each person depicted in the Entry has granted permission to be portrayed as shown. Any costumes, props or other materials used must be rented or borrowed with the permission of the owner, and all other relevant permissions must have been obtained.

4.4 In accordance with clause 3.2 and 3.3 all shortlisted and winning photographers will be contacted by email. If the World Photography Organisation does not hear from the entrant by the date specified in any correspondence and is therefore not able to ratify the entry that entrant will be disqualified and replaced by another photographer.

5.1 If you are under 16, you have Your parent’s or legal guardian’s consent to participate in the Competition.

5.2 If the World Photography Organisation does not receive a valid signed parental or legal guardian consent form for any winner under the age of 16 within 7 clear days of the Entrant being declared a winner (excluding the day on which such declaration is made by the World Photography Organisation ) the World Photography Organisation will be entitled to select an alternative winner from among the Entrants.

6. The World Photography Organisation may run an online rating process whereby members of the public may vote for a favourite photograph. If there is sufficient evidence (in the World Photography Organisation’s sole discretion) to suggest malpractice and manipulation of the rating process, then the World Photography Organisation has the right to remove the relevant Entry or Entries and, if necessary, award the prize to a different Entrant. the World Photography Organisation’s decisions are final.

7.1 The World Photography Organisation recognises You, the author of the image, retain full ownership of the copyright in each Entry.

7.2 All Entrants understand that any image submitted to the competition may be used by the World Photography Organisation, and its Event Partners, for marketing and promotional purposes of You the author and the event only, for a maximum of three years after the announcement in April 2027. You hereby grant the World Photography Organisation a non-exclusive, irrevocable licence in each Entry throughout the world for three years in all media for any use connected to the promotion of You the author and the Sony World Photography Awards event and/or competition, including, but not limited too:

(a) judging the Competition

(b) displaying the winning entries and runners up at public exhibitions promoting the World Photography Organisation and organised by the World Photography Organisation

(c) inclusion within the Website, a World Photography Awards book, magazine or similar

(d) inclusion within any materials promoting of the Competition and / or any exhibition organised by the World Photography Organisation , in the promotion of the World Photography Organisation

(e) inclusion on Competition- and exhibition-related products to be sold by the World Photography Organisation or any third party following the individual agreement by the author

(f) sub-licensing the Entries to the press for reproduction in connection with the Competition and any exhibition

(g) allowing viewers of the Website and/or Sony World Photography Awards Application to view images on a computer screen, PDA or mobile telephone and store such pages in electronic form on disk or on a PDA or mobile telephone (but not on any server or other storage device connected to a network) for their personal, non-commercial use only. Please also refer to clause 9.

(h) incorporation by the World Photography Organisation and Sony World Photography Awards Event Partners in Sony World Photography Awards Galleries and or Sony World Photography Awards Gallery Applications on Event Partner devices for a period of three (3) years after the applicable announcement date. Notwithstanding the foregoing, You hereby acknowledge and agree if Your image is included in such Sony World Photography Awards Galleries or Sony World Photography Awards Gallery Applications Your image will remain perpetually in the device royalty free.

7.3 All Entrants understand that the image information, including image name and description, may be shared with Event partners and media as per clause 7.1, 7.2 and 8. For the avoidance of doubt the “image information” does not include any personal information of You the author.

7.3.1 Should entrants elect to opt-in to sharing data, the email data and name will be shared with our event partners.

7.4 All entrants are required to enter under their correct names, and all entrants are responsible for providing this information accurately. The Awards programme is structured around providing opportunities and exposure to individual photographers and as such we do not award anonymously or accept pseudonyms.

7.5 The World Photography Organisation reserves the right to select which images be featured within the curated exhibit and such curation is made in its sole discretion. Associated image captions and bios may also be edited to fit within the context of the exhibition, book or other material connected to the Awards.

7.6 For Entrants that qualify for the National & Regional Award programme, the Promoter reserves the right not to award a winner if, in the opinion of the judges, none of the Entrants meet the required standard.

8. Any photograph used by the World Photography Organisation shall carry a credit line. Any failure to provide such credit line shall not be deemed to be a breach, as long as the World Photography Organisation uses its reasonable endeavours to rectify such failure within a reasonable period from the date of notice of such failure.

8a. All entrants understand the World Photography Organisation may need to crop your image or add text or logos when used specifically to promote your work or the Awards for online promotional purposes only.

9. The World Photography Organisation assumes no responsibility for any incorrect, inaccurate or incomplete information, whether caused by website users or by any of the equipment or programming associated with or utilised in the Competition, and the World Photography Organisation assumes no responsibility for technical, hardware or software failures of any kind, for lost network connections, garbled computer transmissions, other problems or technical malfunctions with regard to the Competition. The World Photography Organisation assumes no responsibility for any error, omission, corruption, interruption, deletion, defect, delay in operation or transmission, communications line failure, theft or destruction or unauthorized access to or alteration of Entries. the World Photography Organisation is not responsible for any problems or technical malfunction of any telephone network or lines, computer on-line systems, servers, computer equipment, software, failure of any e-mail addressed to the World Photography Organisation on account of technical problems, human error or traffic congestion on the internet or any website, or any combination thereof, including any injury or damage to Your or any other person's computer related to or resulting from participation or downloading any materials in the Competition. If for any reason a contestant’s entry cannot be viewed or is not capable of running as planned, including infection by computer viruses, bugs, tampering, unauthorized intervention, fraud or technical failures, the World Photography Organisation assumes no responsibility.

10. In no event will the World Photography Organisation , its parents, affiliates, subsidiaries and related companies, Event Partners, its advertising or promotion agencies, or its officers, directors, employees, shareholders, representatives or agents be responsible or liable for any damages or losses of any kind, including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, special or punitive damages arising out of any Entrant’s access to and use of the Website. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, everything on the Website is provided "as is"without warranty of any kind, either expressed or implied, including but not limited to, the implied warranty of merchantability, fitness for purpose or use or non-infringement.

11. You agree to participate in related publicity and to the use of Your name and likeness for the purposes of advertising, promotion and publicity without additional compensation.

12. If shortlisted entrants are unable to supply a high resolution image of at least 5MB and 300ppi their entry may be disqualified.

13. There are no cash alternatives available for prize winners.

13.1 Prize winners may receive digital imaging equipment as part of their prize and in such cases equipment may be sent to them. In some countries income tax may be applicable to prizes. It is the winner’s responsibility to pay any income taxes related to the prize in compliance with their own country’s law. In such cases the Winner agrees to indemnify and keep the World Photography Organisation, its parents, affiliates or partners indemnified against any tax liability, charges, fines, penalties or interest or any other liability incurred by the winner which liability arose as a result of prizes provided to the Winner.

13.1.i Valid ETAs or Standard Visas to the UK are needed to attend the ceremony. It is the responsibility of the Entrant to acquire their own visa or entry forms. The Promoter is not responsible for the cost of the Entrant’s visa application and entry forms.

14. Winner will be announced online and at a black-tie ceremony in London.

editorial_title_zh: Galerie Le Château d’Eau：摄影的生命史
editorial_excerpt_zh: 在图卢兹，多亏了雷城堡水塔画廊（Château d’Eau），摄影正回归其根源。作为摄影二百周年（Bicentenaire de la […] 这篇文章最初发表在《摄影之眼》（The Eye of Photography Magazine）。
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "在图卢兹，多亏了雷城堡水塔画廊（Château d’Eau），摄影正回归其根源。作为摄影二百周年（Bicentenaire de la Photographie）官方项目的一部分，这家著名的画廊将其自身的收藏与该市另外两处历史馆藏结合进行对话：保罗-迪皮伊珍贵艺术博物馆（musée des Arts Précieux Paul-Dupuy）和乔治-拉比特博物馆（musée Georges-Labit）。这场活动堪称此前从未共处一室的作品之间的一场真正对话。雷城堡水塔画廊建于首批化学工艺诞生之际，是一座举足轻重的机构，自1974年以来，它遵照创始人让·迪厄扎德（Jean Dieuzaide）的意愿，在法国传播并捍卫摄影创作。这次合作的成果是一段精彩的旅程，兼具时间顺序与主题性。它从19世纪摄影的诞生一直延伸到当下的最新实验，在所有维度上探索影像。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "起点将我们直接带回著名的“鸽子屋景观”（Point de vue du Gras），这是尼谢福尔·涅普斯（Nicéphore Niépce）于1827年定格的影像，如今被视为历史上的第一张照片。以这件奠基之作为起点，展览巧妙地追溯了从单纯的机械工具向成熟创作空间的过渡。这是一个理解以下事实的契机：同时驾驭光线、感光介质和光学能够诞生一种拥有自身密码的视觉语言，从而彻底改变我们的表征模式。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "旅程的其余部分审视了摄影永恒的两面性。这门艺术在纯粹的审美探索与作为文档的自然功能之间无休止地撕扯。无论是延伸了它们的取向还是刻意对其形成冲击。在这里，摄影与绘画和雕塑并肩而立，但除了这种形式上的对话，展览突显了它作为世界见证者的核心作用。正是这种捕捉现实瞬间、展现濒临消失之物或归档我们集体记忆的独一无二的能力，深深触动了观者。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "最后，漫步以一个更具本土特色的音符结束，聚焦于这座红砖画廊的历史。其非凡的收藏见证了折衷的相遇与艺术的选择。这里对人道主义摄影有着深厚的情结，同时也存在将我们与美国和西班牙艺术界连接起来的文化纽带。总而言之，这场大型回顾展精彩地向我们展示了摄影是一种充满生命的媒介、一场永恒的运动。它是我们理解世界所需的光芒，因为它邀请我们与之共同书写世界。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "让-雅克·阿代尔（Jean-Jacques Ader）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "雷城堡水塔画廊（Galerie Le Château d’Eau），1 place Laganne, Toulouse。“摄影的生命史”（“Les vies de la photographie”）展览，2026年10月17日至2027年2月21日，由娜塔莉·布卢什（Nathalie Boulouch）策展。出版物《Camera Luminaria》，Le Bec en l’air/Le Château d’Eau出版。信息：https://chateaudeau.toulouse.fr/", "links": [{"text": "https://chateaudeau.toulouse.fr/", "url": "https://chateaudeau.toulouse.fr/"}], "translated": true}]

article_text:
In Toulouse, thanks to the Château d’Eau, photography is returning to its roots. As part of the official program of the Bicentenaire de la Photographie , the celebrated gallery sets its own collection in dialogue with two other heritage collections of the city: that of the musée des Arts Précieux Paul-Dupuy and that of the musée Georges-Labit. The event is a true conversation between works that had never before shared the same walls. Built at the time the first chemical processes appeared, the Château d’Eau stands as an essential institution which, in keeping with the wishes of its founder Jean Dieuzaide, has transmitted and defended photographic creation in France since 1974. The result of this collaboration is a superb journey, both chronological and thematic. It runs from photography’s emergence in the nineteenth century to the most current experiments, exploring images in all their dimensions.

The starting point takes us straight back to the famous “ Point de vue du Gras ”, the image fixed by Nicéphore Niépce in 1827 and now considered the very first photograph in history. Starting from this founding work, the exhibition deftly traces the passage from a simple mechanical tool to a fully fledged space for creation. It is an opportunity to understand that mastering light, the sensitive medium and optics together could give birth to a visual language with its own codes, definitively transforming our modes of representation.

The rest of the journey considers photography’s permanent ambivalence. An art endlessly torn between pure aesthetic research and its natural function as document. Whether it extends their approach or deliberately jostles it. Photography here rubs shoulders with painting and sculpture, but beyond this formal dialogue, the exhibition highlights its essential role as witness to the world. It is this unique capacity to capture moments of reality, to show what is on the verge of disappearing, or to archive our collective memory that leaps out at the viewer.

Finally, the stroll ends on a more local note, centered on the history of the red-brick gallery. Its exceptional collection bears witness to eclectic encounters and artistic choices. There is a deep attachment to humanist photography, but also cultural ties linking us to the American and Spanish art worlds. All in all, this major retrospective shows us brilliantly that photography is a living medium, a permanent movement. It is a light we need in order to understand the world, since it invites us to write it with her.

Jean-Jacques Ader

Galerie Le Château d’Eau, 1 place Laganne, Toulouse. Exhibition “Les vies de la photographie,” October 17, 2026, through February 21, 2027, curated by Nathalie Boulouch. Publication of the book “Camera Luminaria,” Le Bec en l’air/Le Château d’Eau. Information: https://chateaudeau.toulouse.fr/

article_text:
「週刊少年ジャンプ」で2020年より連載中の大ヒット漫画『SAKAMOTO DAYS』の大型原作展「SAKAMOTO DAYS展」名古屋会場が、テレピアホール（名古屋市東区）で11月23日まで開催中です。

本展覧会では、カラーイラストを含む1７0点以上の完成原稿展示に加え、初公開となる秘蔵資料を含む直筆創作資料９0点以上を公開！作者・鈴木祐斗氏の激しくも美しいイラストを基軸に、展示造作や空間構成をダイナミックに展開しています。 さらに、作者・鈴木祐斗氏からの直筆メッセージ色紙を名古屋会場から展示しています。また、名古屋会場から登場の新グッズも好評販売中です。

名古屋会場新グッズ

腰掛けアクリルスタンド（坂本太郎、朝倉シン、南雲与市）各1,650円 購入個数制限:各2個

フルカラーアートボードEx 南雲与市VS楽 5,940円 購⼊個数制限: 2個

缶マグネット2個セット(57mmサイズ) 有月憬＆赤尾リオン 1,320円 購⼊個数制限: 2個

SAKAMOTO DAYS展 名古屋会場

会期：2026年10月3日（土）～11月23日（月・祝） ※会期中無休

会場：テレピアホール（名古屋市東区東桜1丁目14−25 テレピアビル 2F）

アクセス：地下鉄東山線・名城線「栄」駅、名鉄瀬戸線「栄町」駅下車、4A番出口より東へ徒歩5分 地下鉄桜通線「高岳」駅下車、南へ徒歩5分 市バス「東新町」下車

開場時間：10:00～17:00（最終入場16:30）

チケット料金：一般2,000円 中学・高校生1,500円 小学生900円 グッズ付（数量限定）4,200円

お問い合わせ：SAKAMOTO DAYS展名古屋事務局 090-9712-7096（会期中10:00～17:00）

editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Auseklis", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Auseklis是拉脱维亚神话中的晨星和黎明之神。受雪、流亡者和里加的日出启发，一个名为Auseklis的项目讲述了一个关于看见星辰、做梦和重新创造神话与传说片段的短篇故事。“如果你在冬季的星期五发现了一些石头，它们可能覆盖着那些曾经白日做梦之人的古老文字……一只迷失在大城市的兔子承载着与森林之树相遇的信息。Auskelis已逃离噩梦的喧嚣，正在黑暗中等待，等待一个信号，以便在天际线上现身……”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "里加拉脱维亚ISSP驻地项目 数码摄影 2022", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Auseklis

Auseklis is the morning star and deity of the dawn in latvian mythology. Getting inspired by the snow, the diaspora and sunrises in Riga, a project titled Auseklis is a short story about seeing the stars, dreaming, and re-creating glimpses of myths and legends. “If you find some rocks on Friday in the winter season, they are possibly covered with ancient texts of people who daydreamed… A rabbit lost in the big city carries the messages of meeting the trees of the forest. Auskelis has fled from the noise of the nightmares and is waiting, in the darkness, for a sign to make his appearance in the skyline…”

Residency Project at ISSP, Riga Latvia Digital Photography 2022

title_original: What Do You Get When the ‘Texas Chainsaw’ Director Takes on the Marquis de Sade? The Kinky Pleasures of ‘Night Terrors’
editorial_title_zh: 当《德州电锯杀人狂》导演遇上萨德侯爵会碰撞出什么？《午夜惊魂》的背德乐趣
editorial_excerpt_zh: 托比·霍珀这部被遗忘且饱受诟病的恐怖与软色情混合之作推出蓝光碟，全景展现其全裸骑马、舞蛇和挖眼等种种奇观，正赶上万圣节之际。
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "导演托比·霍珀既是恐怖片界最负盛名的电影人之一，也是最被低估的导演之一——之所以备受赞誉，是因为他执导了影史上最具影响力、最成功的恐怖片之一《德州电锯杀人狂》；而说他被低估，则是因为他之后的大多数作品普遍缺乏应有的欣赏。霍珀的最大热门作品《鬼驱人》的功劳通常（且错误地）被归功于制片人斯蒂芬·斯皮尔伯格。此外，尽管霍珀的电视剧版《撒冷镇》近年来地位有所上升，但他总体上仍被视为活在《德州电锯杀人狂》阴影下的导演——如果人们还会讨论他的话。", "links": [{"text": "Tobe Hooper", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/features/general/tobe-hooper-best-films-the-texas-chain-saw-massacre-poltergeist-1201870176/"}, {"text": "The Texas Chainsaw Massacre", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/features/interviews/the-texas-chain-saw-massacre-turns-50-leatherface-1235033174/"}, {"text": "Steven Spielberg", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/features/general/the-fabelmans-easter-eggs-spielberg-1234784145/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/DSC_8200.jpg?w=300&h=168&crop=1", "alt": "2026年 Slamdance 编剧比赛的获奖者于2026年10月27日与 Slamdance 总裁兼创始人彼得·巴克斯特、电影节经理安娜·李·劳森以及 AGBO 电影与电视高级副总裁阿里·科斯塔合影", "caption": "", "credit": "IndieWire", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/GettyImages-167944112.jpg?w=300&h=168&crop=1", "alt": "约翰·卡彭特", "caption": "", "credit": "IndieWire", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "然而，在霍珀拍摄《德州电锯杀人狂》之后的一十多部故事片中，有几部确实极其独特——正如那部充满忧郁与不安情绪的1981年砍杀电影《游乐场惊魂》一样——在各自的恐怖片子类型中堪称顶尖。其中有些电影不仅被遗忘，而且最初就鲜为人知，考虑到霍珀在1990年代和2000年代如同白蚁般的存在——几十年来在低成本直供DVD的独立电影以及匿名的有线电视委制项目中默默耕耘。", "links": [{"text": "film", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/t/film/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "值得庆幸的是，像 Arrow、Shout! Factory 和 Vinegar Syndrome 这样的精品实体媒介厂牌在过去几年里一直在给予这位导演作品应有的尊重，推出了附带丰富花絮的4K UHD和蓝光碟，涵盖了《活食》、《游乐场惊魂》和《机械绞肉机》等霍珀的核心电影。现在，Vinegar Syndrome 推出了霍珀1993年取材自萨德侯爵作品的改编之作《午夜惊魂》的精美特别版，这部电影堪称这位导演最受诟病的电影之一。它同时也是他最好的作品之一。", "links": [{"text": "Vinegar Syndrome", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/t/vinegar-syndrome/"}, {"text": "Night Terrors", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/t/night-terrors/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《午夜惊魂》之所以如此有趣且高度契合霍珀的关注点和风格母题，其实有点令人意外，因为这是导演在项目后期才相对较晚接手的一个委制任务。该片最初源自哈里·艾伦·托尔斯，一位说得好听点有着丰富多彩过往的制片人——在1960年代，他曾是个据传闻的苏联间谍，经营着一个负责诱捕并勒索美国高级官员（包括时任总统约翰·F·肯尼迪）的色情团伙。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "到了《夜惊》（Night Terrors）问世之时，塔尔斯已是一位制作过数十部故事片的制片人，其中包括几部改编自萨德侯爵作品的电影。《夜惊》最初是对其中一部电影的重新构思——即1969年的《尤金妮……她走向堕落之旅》（Eugenie…The Story of Her Journey into Perversion），但当塔尔斯在20世纪90年代初与以色列制片人约拉姆·格洛布斯（Yoram Globus）合作时，它演变成了一部截然不同的作品。当时的设想是，这位曾与梅纳赫姆·戈兰（Menahem Golan）长期合作、如今分道扬镳的坎农影业（Cannon Films）大亨将与塔尔斯联手，把《尤金妮》重制为一部恐怖片。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "戈布us与霍珀曾有过合作历史，坎农影业曾在1980年代资助了这位导演资金最充裕——也是商业上最不成功——的三部故事片。在霍珀凭借1982年的《鬼驱人》大获成功后，他与坎农签下一笔交易，拍出了《宇宙天魔》、《火星人入侵》和《德州电锯杀人狂2》。这三部作品虽是艺术上的胜利，却也是经济上的灾难，加速了坎农的消亡，并基本上断送了霍珀手握充足预算拍片的职业生涯。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "尽管电影票房失利，且在极其昂贵的《宇宙天魔》中有过一些高管干预，霍珀和戈布us双方依然合作愉快。事实上，尽管坎农顶着剥削片大本营的名声，它却是一家极其尊重电影人的机构。除了诸如《霹雳怡红院2》和《猛龙怪客3》这样的最低共同分母式的大众货外，他们还资助了约翰·卡萨维茨（《爱流》）、罗伯特·奥特曼（《爱情痴狂》）和让-吕克·戈达尔（《李尔王》）等作者导演的项目，并赋予这些导演几乎完全的创作控制权。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "霍珀也不例外，他将始于《电锯杀人狂》的对美国文化和价值观的常规批判，夹带进了大预算的《宇宙天魔》和《火星人入侵》（以及预算稍具理性的《电锯杀人狂2》）中，且并未削弱其观点的锋芒。然而，尽管霍珀与戈布us很合得来，他并不是《午夜惊魂》最初的导演——这一荣誉本来属于英国行活导演格里·奥哈拉。", article_text:
Director Tobe Hooper is simultaneously one of horror’s most celebrated filmmakers and one of its most underrated — celebrated thanks to his direction of one of the most influential and accomplished horror movies of all time, “ The Texas Chainsaw Massacre ,” but underrated given the overall lack of appreciation for most of what came after. Credit for Hooper’s biggest hit, “Poltergeist,” is generally (and erroneously) attributed to producer Steven Spielberg . Elsewhere, though Hooper’s TV adaptation of “Salem’s Lot” has gained stature in recent years, he’s generally discussed as a director whose work lives in the shadow of “Chainsaw” — when he’s discussed at all.

Yet among the more than a dozen features Hooper made after “The Texas Chainsaw Massacre” are several truly distinctive works that often — as in the case of the profoundly melancholy and unsettling 1981 slasher film “The Funhouse” — rank among the best in their horror subgenres. Some of these movies are not only forgotten but were barely known to begin with, given Hooper’s termite-like existence in the 1990s and 2000s, decades spent toiling in low-budget straight-to-DVD indies, and anonymous cable television assignments.

Thankfully, boutique physical media labels like Arrow, Shout! Factory, and Vinegar Syndrome have spent the last several years giving the director’s work the respect it deserves, with supplement-laden 4K UHD and Blu-ray releases of essential Hooper films like “Eaten Alive,” “The Funhouse,” and “The Mangler.” Now, Vinegar Syndrome has produced an exquisite special edition of Hooper’s 1993 riff on the Marquis de Sade, “ Night Terrors ,” a film that ranks among the filmmaker’s most maligned movies. It’s also one of his best.

That “Night Terrors” is so interesting and so aligned with Hooper’s preoccupations and stylistic motifs is a little surprising, given that it was a for-hire assignment the director came to relatively late in the proceedings. The movie originated with Harry Alan Towers, a producer with, to put it mildly, a colorful past — in the 1960s he was a reputed Soviet spy who operated a vice ring tasked with luring and blackmailing prominent U.S. officials, including President John F. Kennedy.

By the time “Night Terrors” came around, Towers was a producer with dozens of features on his resume, including several Marquis de Sade adaptations. “Night Terrors” began as a reworking of one of these, 1969’s “Eugenie…The Story of Her Journey into Perversion,” but it evolved into something fairly different by the time Towers partnered with Israeli producer Yoram Globus in the early 1990s. The idea was that the Cannon Films impresario, whose long-time partnership with Menahem Golan had recently ended, would join forces with Towers to remake “Eugenie” as a horror picture.

Globus had a past with Hooper, Cannon having financed three of the director’s most well-resourced — and financially unsuccessful — features in the 1980s. After Hooper hit big with “Poltergeist” in 1982, he signed a deal with Cannon that yielded “Lifeforce,” “Invaders From Mars,” and “Texas Chainsaw Massacre 2,” three artistic triumphs but economic disasters that accelerated Cannon’s demise and essentially put an end to Hooper’s career working with generous budgets.

Hooper and Golan-Globus were happy with each other despite the movies’ box-office failures and a bit of executive meddling on the extremely expensive “Lifeforce.” Cannon was, in fact, an extremely filmmaker-friendly outfit despite its reputation as exploitation schlockmeisters. Alongside bread-and-butter lowest common denominator fare like “Breakin 2: Electric Boogaloo” and “Death Wish III,” they financed auteur projects by John Cassavetes (“Love Streams”), Robert Altman (“Fool For Love”), and Jean-Luc Godard (“King Lear”), and granted those directors almost total creative control.

Hooper was no exception, smuggling his usual critique of American culture and values that began with “Chainsaw” into the big-budget “Lifeforce” and “Invaders of Mars” (and the slightly more reasonably budgeted “Chainsaw 2”), without compromising the ferocity of his point of view. In spite of Hooper’s rapport with Globus, however, he was not the original director of “Night Terrors” — that distinction would go to British journeyman Gerry O’Hara.

O’Hara came on board to direct a script by Daniel Matmor that drew on elements from de Sade’s “Philosophy in the Boudoir” and synthesized them into a very 1990s cocktail of horror, softcore pornography, and philosophical inquiry. The movie is framed by material depicting the Marquis de Sade (played by Freddy Krueger himself, Robert Englund) ranting from his prison cell; this is intercut with a present-day story in which Genie (Zoe Trilling), a young American woman visiting Egypt, is indoctrinated into a sex cult led by one of de Sade’s descendants (also played by Englund).

Conflicting reports surround O’Hara’s departure from the project, but one factor seems to be the switch from Egypt to Israel as a shooting location. This change, driven by financial considerations, also troubled Englund, since his primary motivation for signing on was his desire to see Egypt. When they decided to change locations, Globus and Towers had an unhappy star and no director.

They brought on Hooper largely to appease Englund, who had worked with the director on “Eaten Alive” and the pilot episode of “Freddy’s Nightmares” (and would work with him again on “The Mangler”). He was probably happy for the job, given that whatever commercial capital he had accumulated at Cannon after the success of “Poltergeist” was long gone. Hooper had spent the years since 1986’s “Chainsaw 2” largely in television, with only 1990’s “Spontaneous Combustion” appearing in theaters since.

The director’s late arrival to “Night Terrors” doesn’t show anywhere in the film, which feels like pure, undiluted Hooper; it’s a glorious showcase for his gifts, from the abundantly horrific imagery in de Sade’s imprisonment and torture to the dark, ironic sense of humor that characterizes the scenes depicting the sex cult (scenes that are both funnier and more disturbing in the age of Jeffrey Epstein). Coming in to save the day in the late innings rather than having labored over the project for months or years, Hooper feels liberated in “Night Terrors,” and lets his imagination run wild.

The erotic elements of “Night Terrors” in particular are really something to behold, from a snake-fellating belly dancer and naked horseback riding to the sex party whose guests arrive dressed as children. Hooper has always been marked by his transgressive side, whether in violence, sex, or politics. His films are provocations, and “Night Terrors” is no exception. He’s also always been marked by his sly and aggressive sense of humor, which is put to good use here — in fact, the line between erotic, offensive, and hilarious is often blurred to extremely entertaining effect, as Hooper pushes the outrageousness of Matmor’s script to its limit and beyond.

He also takes his usual sense of intertextual commentary in new directions thanks to the movie’s sexual component. Hooper was always the kind of director, like many of his peers, who was comfortable with referencing other movies and using those references in conversation with his own work to create new meanings. The kids in “Salem’s Lot,” “Poltergeist,” and “Invaders From Mars” all live in shrines to pop culture that inform and reflect their own lives, and even the killer in “The Funhouse” has a special relationship with Frankenstein’s monster.

In “Night Terrors,” Hooper creates a dialogue not only with other horror movies, but with the erotic films and TV shows that proliferated in the late 1980s and early 1990s. The story of Genie’s sexual awakening has more than a little in common with Zalman King-scripted soft-core fare like “9 1/2 Weeks,” “Two Moon Junction,” and “Red Shoe Diaries,” and Hooper borrows the highly diffused neon lighting and ad agency-inspired aesthetic of those works for his own sex scenes. Yet he also constantly undercuts or plays against them with satire, gore, and just out-and-out weirdness — it’s hard for a soft-core movie to enter the nervous system unimpeded when it’s punctuated with eyeball-gouging and Robert Englund theatrically pontificating while hanging from a cross.

In spite of — or perhaps because of — the everything and the kitchen sink maximalism of Hooper’s approach, “Night Terrors” remains one of his most poorly received films, with a lower IMDb ranking even than 2000’s excoriated “Crocodile” and barely any mention at all in “American Twilight,” the definitive and indispensable text on Hooper’s work. This makes Vinegar Syndrome’s Blu-ray release invaluable, as they’ve meticulously restored the film from an archival print and loaded it with respectful, informative extras. It’s a great way to discover Hooper’s most unfairly neglected film, and to ponder the breadth and depth of his work in general.

The limited edition Blu-ray of Tobe Hooper ‘s “Night Terrors” is now available from Vinegar Syndrome .

article_text:
C inema halls – or dream palaces, as they’re affectionately called – offer a retreat into the realm of make-believe, and everyday drudgery is left at the door. Though set within a single-screen theatre in the Argentinian city of Córdoba, Ramiro Sonzini and Ezequiel Salinas’s hypnotic film invokes a more porous relationship between the screen and its audience. Here, the messiness of life beguilingly sneaks into this domain of fantasies, blurring the borders between public and private spaces.

While the luminous black-and-white cinematography lends a dreamy fuzziness to the images, the narrative concerns are grounded in thorny economic realities. A film projectionist at his local cinema called Pelu (Octavio Bertone) is reassigned to the post of a night watchman due to budget cuts at the city hall. The cinema soon becomes his literal refuge: he moves out of his cramped rented flat and secretly takes up occupation at his workplace. He then welcomes a horde of other outsiders, including his unemployed roommate, an ageing drifter and a sex worker who livestreams her erotic shows from the cinema. Every night, they watch classic films from the old masters – Jean Renoir, Yasujiro Ozu and Robert Bresson to name a few – until the early hours.

Despite these self-referential touches, the film steers clear of nostalgia; cinephilia is transformed into a force for public good, and a conduit to direct action. In the wake of Javier Milei’s election win in 2023 , which ushered in a new era of far-right conservatism, Pelu and his friends’ radical acts of vandalism transform a commercialised space into a restorative commune. In an echo of classic westerns, there’s a galvanising scene where these wayward outcasts gather around a fire to exchange songs and stories. No longer tethered to flickering images on a silver screen, the flames of camaraderie are also alive beyond the frame.

article_text:
O ensaio Camas e lápides , publicado no site do Los Angeles Review of Books, faz uma interessante leitura da retrospectiva da artista francesa Shopie Calle , no Museu Langson, sob a ótica da obra do escritor francês Hervé Guibert .

“A franqueza e a provocação de Guibert, aliadas a uma sutil corrente de distanciamento conceitual, fazem das obras dele e de Calle companheiras naturais. A rejeição da privacidade por parte dela, o desmantelamento das fronteiras burguesas e a insistência esporádica na natureza de objeto da imagem — ressaltadas pela adoção da tecnologia analógica e pelo uso de instalações que remetem à colagem e frequentemente evocam a estrutura de um livro — materializam muitas das questões intrínsecas ao texto de Guibert.”

O site do British Journal of Photography publicou um obituário do fotógrafo britânico Ian Berry , falecido no último dia 13 de setembro, aos 92 anos. O texto destaca uma das fotos mais importantes da carreira de Berry: em 21 de março de 1960, o jovem fotógrafo estava em Sharpeville, um bairro segregado (“township”) na África do Sul, onde cerca de 5.000 a 7.000 pessoas haviam se reunido em frente a uma delegacia de polícia para protestar.

Berry, que morava na África do Sul e trabalhava para a revista Drum , estava lá para documentar o evento junto com outros membros da imprensa, mas nada de dramático parecia estar acontecendo. Até que, de repente, aconteceu. “No início da noite, um comboio de veículos blindados da polícia avançou pelas ruas da localidade, e eu, juntamente com outros fotógrafos e jornalistas, seguimos logo atrás. Mas logo recebemos ordens para nos dispersar”, conta o fotógrafo.

A exposição Robert Mapplethorpe : As formas da beleza , em cartaz no Museo dell’Ara Pacis, em Roma, reúne mais de 200 fotografias que cobrem grande parte da trajetória do fotógrafo americano. A mostra explora a precisão formal subjacente à obra de Mapplethorpe. O artista transforma corpos, retratos e naturezas-mortas em formas que remetem à escultura clássica, estabelecendo um diálogo entre a fotografia contemporânea e a arte antiga.

“O foco na técnica precisa de Robert Mapplethorpe — caracterizada pela iluminação controlada, pela simetria e pela composição — revela um artista em busca da perfeição visual. As formas da beleza é singular ao demonstrar como suas imagens mais modernas permanecem conectadas a noções muito mais antigas de proporção, harmonia e idealização do corpo.”

Ensaio publicado no site do jornal japonês Pen aborda o fascínio de Daido Moriyama pela fotografia mais antiga do mundo, que este ano celebra o seu bicentenário. “ Vista da janela de Le Gras , feita pelo inventor francês Nicéphore Niépce em 1826 ou 1827 na sua casa em Saint-Loup-de-Varennes, na Borgonha, é nada menos que um milagre. É a fotografia mais antiga que conhecemos. Resultado de uma experiência ainda mais próxima da invenção científica do que da criação artística, a imagem fascina Daido Moriyama desde que a descobriu numa revista em meados da década de 1970.”

Um possível renascimento da fotografia? É o que se pergunta o pesquisador e crítico norte-americano Fred Ritchin em ensaio publicado em sua newsletter do Substack. Ritchin investiga a possibilidade de a IA fotorrealista ter perdido muito do seu brilho inicial.

“Como um dos primeiros a utilizar essas ferramentas, percebi que os sistemas de IA convencionais com os quais trabalhava anos atrás frequentemente respondiam aos comandos de texto de maneiras idiossincráticas, e até reveladoras, que eu não poderia ter previsto. Muitas vezes, eu me via surpreso — e até inquieto — com as imagens produzidas, mas isso já não acontece mais.”

Por ocasião da exposição Man Ray : Tudo , em cartaz na Fundação Magnani Rocca em Parma. O Giornale Dell’Arte entrevistou Walter Guadagnini, um dos curadores da mostra, ao lado Mauro Carrera e Stefano Roffi. Organizada 50 anos após a morte de um dos artistas mais brilhantes e versáteis do século 20, a exposição reúne algumas de suas obras-primas, como Le Violon d’Ingres (1924), retratando Kiki de Montparnasse (Alice Ernestine Prin), bem como os famosos retratos das musas e modelos Lee Miller e Nusch Éluard.

Matéria publicada no site The Art-Journal repercute a notícia publicada no início de agosto pela imprensa alemã de que a renomada editora Steidl Verlag havia entrado com um pedido de insolvência. Na visão do Art-Journal , “a notícia foi particularmente preocupante porque a Steidl é amplamente considerada a principal editora de monografias fotográficas do mundo. Se até mesmo a Steidl enfrenta dificuldades, o que isso sugere sobre o restante do setor?”

18世紀、南米。イエズス会の宣教師ガブリエル神父は、音楽を通して先住民のグアラニー族と心を通わせ、平和な共同体を築いていた。一方、奴隷商人ロドリゴ・メンドーサは、ある悲劇をきっかけに、自らの罪を償う道を歩み始める。しかし、植民地政策の変化によって宣教地は存続の危機に直面し、2人の信念は大きく揺さぶられていく。武器を取る者と、祈りを貫く者。それぞれの選択は、やがて悲劇的な運命へとつながっていく。 ミッション

劇場公開日： 2026年10月16日

映画館を探す

予告編を見る

U-NEXTで 本編を見る PR

解説・あらすじ

18世紀の南米を舞台に、宣教師と奴隷商人の生き方を通して人間の良心と信念を描いたイギリス・フランス合作映画で、1986年の第39回カンヌ国際映画祭でパルムドールに輝いた歴史ドラマ。 18世紀、南米。イエズス会の宣教師ガブリエル神父は、音楽を通して先住民のグアラニー族と心を通わせ、平和な共同体を築いていた。一方、奴隷商人ロドリゴ・メンドーサは、ある悲劇をきっかけに、自らの罪を償う道を歩み始める。しかし、植民地政策の変化によって宣教地は存続の危機に直面し、2人の信念は大きく揺さぶられていく。武器を取る者と、祈りを貫く者。それぞれの選択は、やがて悲劇的な運命へとつながっていく。 ガブリエル神父をジェレミー・アイアンズ、メンドーサをロバート・デ・ニーロが演じ、エイダン・クイン、リーアム・ニーソンらが共演。監督は「キリング・フィールド」「シティ・オブ・ジョイ」で知られるローランド・ジョフィ、脚本は「ドクトル・ジバゴ」「アラビアのロレンス」のロバート・ボルト。クリス・メンゲスの撮影は第59回アカデミー賞撮影賞を受賞。エンニオ・モリコーネによる「ガブリエルのオーボエ」をはじめとする音楽も映画音楽史に残る名曲として親しまれている。2026年、公開40周年を記念して4Kデジタルリマスター版で再公開される。

1986年製作／126分／G／イギリス・フランス合作 原題または英題：The Mission 配給：アークエンタテインメント 劇場公開日：2026年10月16日

その他の公開日：1987年4月18日（日本初公開）

原則として東京で一週間以上の上映が行われた場合に掲載しています。 ※映画祭での上映や一部の特集、上映・特別上映、配給会社が主体ではない上映企画等で公開されたものなど掲載されない場合もあります。

article_text:
The first reactions are in for DC Comics ‘ body horror thriller “ Clayface ,” with journalists and fans calling it “freakishly awesome” and “everything you want from a villain-led movie.”

Directed by “Speak No Evil” filmmaker James Watkins from a screenplay co-written by “The Haunting of Hill House” creator Mike Flanagan , “Clayface” stars Tom Rhys Harries as the DC Universe character and Batman adversary. Clayface is Matt Hagen, an actor whose face is disfigured by a local mob boss. Desperate, he volunteers as a test subject for scientist Dr. Caitlyn Corr (Naomi Ackie), who transforms his body into clay and causes him to lose his sanity.

Related Stories

'Children of Blood and Bone' Author Tomi Adeyemi Quietly Cancels New York Comic Con Panel

‘Blade Runner 2099’ Trailer: Michelle Yeoh, Hunter Schafer Are Fugitives in Amazon Limited Series

“‘Clayface’ was fantastic,” Collider editor-in-chief Steven Weintraub wrote on X. “An awesome addition to the DCU that doesn’t require any knowledge of DC to enjoy. It’s hard R and loaded with brutal scenes that really surprised me. Audience freaked out a few times during my screening to what was being depicted on screen.”

Film critic Peter Gray added that it “has that comic book flair” but that doesn’t “diminish how BRUTAL it is! Dark, violent, with little levity to offset the nastiness, this is an exciting addition to Gunn’s DCU.” He added that Harries “brings equal boyish charm and quiet menace to the role.”

YouTuber Brandon Davis called the film “freakishly awesome” and praised Watkins for getting “creative with Clayface’s abilities.” He added that Harries “is a star” and “kills it.”

With a story by Flanagan and screenplay co-written by Flanagan and Hossein Amini, “Clayface” also stars David Dencik, Max Minghella and Eddie Marsan and is produced by “The Batman” director Matt Reeves alongside James Gunn and Peter Safran. It’s set to hit U.S. theaters via Warner Bros . on Oct. 23.

See all the first reactions below.

article_text:
Art Review

Who’s the Thief in Deana Lawson’s Photography?

I wonder what the women standing perpetually accused and anonymous might say about the sale of their stolen images.

For her latest show, Deana Lawson made one simple request: no photography allowed. I watched as other gallery-goers entered and received the same mandate, while an attendant handed out Gagosian-branded stickers to cover phone cameras. I found myself watching the crowd, observing micro-expressions of discomfort and surprise.

I imagine the rule against photography in our highly visual, largely immediate world can be unsettling, but is our attachment really that strong? In a society where most of us carry the vehicle of modern technological warfare in our pockets, Lawson’s prohibition on photography is certainly a sensible request. As I looked at the sticker plastered over my own camera, I felt that perhaps that sense of unmooring is precisely Lawson’s point.

Because I couldn’t take photos, as I thought about how to compose my thoughts for this piece, I found myself questioning my sight. This led me to then question my memory, my ability to hold onto the details that my phone usually carries. By the time I left, I wondered: Would I be able to recall the faces, the snapshots on display? Should I? In deference to Lawson’s vision, would I have to relinquish any desire writhing within me for a sense of control through these photographic constraints?

In Edge Control , an ongoing series that began in 2023, Lawson turns her attention to the ubiquity of everyday monitoring as it appears in the genre of the beauty-supply surveillance photo. These photos are typically pinned behind counters to deter theft, a long-held ritual of humiliation. In a recent interview , Lawson said of this work, “If anything, I feel more identity with the people on the wall — like I’m stealing a picture of them stealing.”

Yet by restricting access to what has become, for many, our second set of eyes, Lawson’s newest series provokes a fraught ethical question: Who truly has the power to authorize or deny access?
